approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates a learned molecule sampler with ordinary graph breeding. An autoregressive SMILES model is first trained on unlabeled molecules and kept as a frozen prior. Each objective gets an adaptable copy that generates one batch, followed by two batches made through graph crossover and atom or bond edits. Accepted neural samples refresh a scored population of up to sixty-four molecules, and a fresh neural sample is forced to participate in breeding at each handoff. Accepted graph descendants then train the adaptable sampler through score-ranked replay, trajectory balance with a learned normalizer, and regularization toward the frozen prior. This reciprocal loop ran repeatedly, but each valid novel graph descendant was sent directly for evaluation, and most scored below its best generating parent.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection to the genetic phase. A Gaussian process learned from this objective's accepted scores uses molecular fingerprints to draw plausible score functions over a fresh pool of offspring from the existing graph operators. Each available evaluation slot takes the best remaining offspring under a new sampled function. The first forced neural-parent offspring at each handoff stays as in the Parent, so the reciprocal exchange remains intact. This lineage has only tested direct submission so far; the new ingredient is selection among genetic offspring before they receive real scores. A related graph-only experiment improved final best scores without improving its parent-beating rate, so the hypothesis here concerns discovering useful upper-tail outcomes within the reciprocal loop, with descendant efficiency measured separately.

hypothesis: Use a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process to choose genetic-phase evaluations by posterior-function maximization over fresh graph offspring pools, retaining the Parent's mandatory first fresh-policy offspring at each graph-cycle handoff.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection and reciprocal feedback reproduce across seeds; offspring efficiency remains weak
finding_summary.insights: Replication rules out missing selector execution or a broken reciprocal handoff as explanations for the weak offspring yield: both mechanisms remain active across all three seeds. It also weakens the original suggestion of improved average child-minus-parent score, which held on the screening seed but not on the two additional seeds. The selector consistently changes which offspring are evaluated, but this does not establish that uncertainty itself improves final scores. The original direct-submission Parent has only one available seed, so the earlier paired score gain of 0.005848 remains a single-seed comparison; the new results establish repeatable execution and describe score variability without establishing a paired multi-seed improvement. Prediction error in the new runs is lower than an archive-mean baseline on four of five objectives, yet nominal 95% latent intervals cover only 80.4% of selected accepted scores overall and 41.9% on sitagliptin_mpo, where prediction MSE is also worse than that baseline. These are informative but uncalibrated predictions on the selected molecules. The molecular assessment shows that ring systems and useful basic-amine chemistry are already available, while leading families still mix conventional scaffolds with reactive substitutions, complicated connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry. That narrows the remaining questions toward reliable discrimination among chemically credible alternatives and broader useful scaffold coverage. Matched Parent replicas and a same-pool mean-only or direct-order comparison are still needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency and uncertainty's contribution.
finding_summary.results: Both additional seeds reproduced the intended selection and feedback behavior. Every one of their 1,800 selected offspring maximized its reconstructed correlated posterior draw, and uncertainty changed 1,671 choices (92.8%) relative to choosing the highest posterior mean. All 190 fits used earlier accepted scores only, all 1,710 eligible fixed-molecule predictions changed after feedback, and all 100 protected neural-to-graph handoffs were preserved. There were 90 later reciprocal cycles and 4,480 nonzero graph-bearing policy updates. The two new mean final-best scores were 0.528301 and 0.517608, compared with 0.516098 in the original run of the same algorithm. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score is 0.520669 with a population standard deviation of 0.005432. The three-seed objective means are 0.458300 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.615427 for deco_hop, 0.999997 for drd2_docking, 0.204624 for median_2 and 0.324997 for sitagliptin_mpo. Only 246 of 1,900 graph descendants in the new runs beat their best generating parent (12.95%), and their mean child-minus-parent score was -0.110567. Across all three runs those quantities are 386 of 2,850 (13.54%) and -0.099708. These are below the original direct-submission Parent's single-seed parent-beating rate of 18.21%; that historical comparison is not a paired three-seed efficiency estimate.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and cyclic-amine chemistry, with useful scaffolds mixed with reactive substitutions and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories each cover every listed objective. Each task digest contains 600 evaluated molecules, including 580 optimizer proposals. These are predominantly connected, branched, ring-bearing organic structures: the taskwise ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9793 to 0.9948 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.9362 to 0.9828. Those are SMILES-text presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.0 to 69.7. The repertoire includes biaryl pyrazoles, indole carboxamides, quinoline ureas, azoles and acylhydrazones, aryl-substituted saturated amines, carbonyl-rich fused heterocycles, and triazolyl azetidines. Ring chemistry and basic amine centres are demonstrably available. The individual high-score families are more concentrated than the variety of the complete proposal sets. Conventional medicinal-chemistry building blocks coexist with oxygen- and nitrogen-halogen bonds, hydrazine/nitroso functionality, unusual short ring closures, and oversized concatenated structures. Consequently, synthetic plausibility is questionable overall and drug-likeness is mixed rather than uniformly poor. No proposed set contains explicit stereocentre annotations: every digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0, even though several depicted saturated cores can have configurational alternatives. The charge-marker rate must not be read as a basic-amine rate; neutral amine SMILES can describe protonatable centres, and nitro groups also produce charge markers. For this replication ticket, the supplied parent_trajectories and focus.parent identify seed 0 of n-cc2d839e347b itself. Comparisons below describe that prior run, not an intervention between different algorithms. Apparent score preferences are associations in the supplied molecular observations; absent chemistry is not evidence that an unobserved replacement would improve the score.

per_task.generated_character: Most proposals are aromatic, moderately sized molecules carrying amides, ureas, methoxy or hydroxy groups and frequent halogen substituents. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9793, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9569 and halogen_rate 0.7966. The seed-1 leader is an N-methyl acetanilide bearing a biaryl-linked pyrazole and a phenol. Seed 2 instead favours methoxyquinoline linked through a urea to isoindoline. Earlier proposals include substituted indole carboxamides related to the initial molecule scoring 0.3051048083696145. These recognizable cores are plausibly accessible, although many neighbouring substitutions are less convincing. Low-scoring material includes tiny fluorinated heteroatom fragments and large, heavily decorated polyaryl structures. Compared with the prior seed-0 high tail of modified indole carboxamides, including unusual amide-nitrogen and cumulated-side-chain chemistry at 0.4219568943587627, the new runs supply more conventional alternative leading cores.
liabilities: The high tail includes an aryl hypochlorite and an aryl sulfur-chlorine group, which introduce reactive bonds despite favourable recorded scores.
A chloromethyl substituent occurs in a leading indole derivative. Large conjugated or multiply decorated late products add synthetic complexity without preserving the favourable score range.
The leading aromatic series carries substantial aromatic surface and limited saturated shape variation; this is a structural description, not a measured solubility or exposure result.
missing_features: Broader stable variants preserving the useful phenol, amide and heteroaryl arrangement are poorly represented relative to peripheral halogen and heteroatom substitutions in the leading families.

Controlled changes of core and linker geometry that retain the compact high-score arrangement remain incompletely explored. The observations establish distinct useful core families, but do not identify a uniquely required missing scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic biaryl-pyrazole acetanilide scores 0.5256780516063334; its otherwise corresponding unsubstituted aryl analogue scores 0.4865761385111112. The oxygen-chlorinated analogue scores 0.49263201457052164, so the observed best local substitution is an ordinary hydroxyl group. The related sulfur-chlorine structure scores 0.4686060677105447. Seed 2 reaches 0.427264458706691 with the fluoroquinoline urea, and its final hydroxyquinoline urea scores 0.4219568943587627. At the other extreme, the tiny nitrogen-fluorine fragment scores 0.0, while the large methoxy-rich sulfonamide/polyamine conjugate scores 6.660632986075464e-46. Late enlarged structures still score 0.00022579574859513555 and 0.004904478066078471. The visible preference is for a coherent aromatic core with a limited polar-group arrangement and controlled size; neither halogen addition nor continued growth is uniformly rewarded.

per_task.generated_character: The high-score molecules are conjugated, nitrogen-rich heteroaromatics rather than small aliphatic structures. Seed 2 produces a quinoline-oxadiazole assembly joined by a formamidine-like linkage to a multiply fluorinated aromatic ring; seed 1 produces substituted quinoline acylhydrazones terminating in nitro-containing diazines. Other upper examples contain fused nitrogen/oxygen heterocycles. The digest records aromatic_atom_rate 0.9828, ring_closure_rate 0.9897, mean_smiles_length 69.7 and max_smiles_length 173, consistent with extensive ring chemistry and a sizeable elaborated tail. Its charged_rate 0.3121 includes charge-separated functional groups such as nitro, and does not demonstrate a population of protonated amines. Individual azoles, aryl amides and hydrazones are recognizable synthetic motifs, but extended nitrogen linkages and reactive substitutions make the ensemble questionable. The prior seed-0 leader instead used a conjugated oxygen heterocycle with oxygen- and sulfur-containing heteroaryl appendages and scored 0.6295439524124257.
liabilities: Acylhydrazones and formamidine-like connections introduce tautomeric or configurational alternatives without corresponding geometric specification in the cited structures.
An oxygen-fluorine bond appears in both a leading quinoline derivative and a late enlarged analogue. This is different chemistry from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine.

Nitro-containing heteroaromatics, densely conjugated nitrogen-rich assemblies, and further concatenation warrant chemical-stability and synthetic scrutiny; the recorded score does not establish either property.
missing_features: Stable, geometrically specified alternatives to the imine, hydrazone and extended nitrogen linkages are not established among the supplied leaders. Short polar linkage geometry appears useful, but these observations do not identify a required replacement chemistry.

The high tail has limited evidence for useful saturated shape variation. The equal score of the aromatic and ring-expanded leading pair prevents claiming that additional aromaticity itself is a missing requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The quinoline-oxadiazole/formamidine leader and its fused-ring-expanded, partly nonaromatic analogue both score 0.608457551958113. The nitrodiazine acylhydrazone reaches 0.6082806347691206, and replacing the formamidine-like linkage with an enamine-like connection gives 0.606012284431845. These observations support short polar connections between heteroaromatic regions, while showing that this high-score neighbourhood does not strongly distinguish several chemically different changes. A simple fluoromethane fragment scores 0.5. The more ordinarily makeable aryl sulfone-linked amide scores 0.26999666722212967, and the sulfonylhydrazone scores 0.2969569015725102; synthetic familiarity alone therefore does not explain this gradient. A long nitrogen-rich conjugate scores 0.3298125254720826. Late extended analogues reach 0.597892888498683 and 0.5811424248155854, below the leading compact connected heteroaryl arrangements. The new best is below the prior seed-0 best despite the changed heteroaromatic families.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules combine halogenated aromatic surfaces with saturated nitrogen rings and accessible aliphatic amines. Seed 2 favours arylpiperidines connected through aminoalkyl chains to another aromatic group or to a benzodioxane-like ring system. Seed 1 includes a diaryl ether bearing linked piperidine and pyrrolidine rings. These are medium-sized, recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures, although some variants acquire imines or unusual bridged ring closures. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9948, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9793 and halogen_rate 0.7897. Its low charged_rate of 0.0121 does not mean basic centres are scarce: the neutral SMILES explicitly contain secondary and tertiary amines. The prior seed-0 leader was a more compact fused aza-polycyclic structure with an N-propyl substituent and an aryl fluoride, scoring 0.9999968262975905. The new high tail is often more extended while retaining the same broad amine-plus-aromatic character.
liabilities: Several leading structures have multiple basic centres, flexible aminoalkyl chains and heavily halogenated aromatic regions. These raise plausible physicochemical concerns without supplying measured protonation, solubility or selectivity evidence.

Some high-scoring variants contain extra short closures across an aromatic ring or unusually bridged oxygen-containing ring systems; a chemically valid graph does not establish an accessible, unstrained structure.
Late sulfur-nitrogen substitutions and imine additions can alter the electronic character of otherwise useful amines. Relevant saturated centres are not stereochemically specified.
missing_features: No additional objective-required functional group can be identified from the near-ceiling high tail; saturated basic centres and aromatic binding surfaces are already represented.

Systematically controlled linker geometry and configurationally specified saturated-ring variants are not demonstrated. Their absence limits the chemical interpretation of shape changes, but the trajectories do not establish that adding them would raise this score.

By contrast, the acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen-rich aromatic molecule scores 3.8021829379963674e-05 and the cyclic thione/carbonyl structure scores 0.0001124209367987908. A nitro-containing heteroaromatic molecule carrying a primary aminomethyl group still scores only 8.914135292267243e-05: having an amine somewhere is insufficient. A late piperidine sulfenamide scores 0.00292826144046475, while an oversized connected amine/aryl assembly scores 0.2524472505210873. These complete-molecule comparisons associate the high scores with accessible saturated amines in appropriate aryl/linker arrangements, not merely nitrogen or ring abundance. The near-ceiling upper values occur for both the prior compact core and the new extended families.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists largely of bulky, densely functionalized ring systems: substituted aromatic groups carry piperazine units alongside fused or rearranged nitrogen heterocycles with carbonyl and ether functionality. Seed 1 often sulfonylates a piperazine nitrogen and adds cyclopropyl or cyclopropenyl groups; seed 2 includes N-methylpiperazine-containing relatives of the initial diaryl fused dicarbonyl heterocycle. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9552, mean_smiles_length 64.1 and max_smiles_length 163. Aromatic rings, saturated nitrogen rings and heterocyclic carbonyl groups are all plentiful. Many building blocks are conventional, but the complete leading structures combine substantial size with complicated fused or contracted connectivity. Prior seed 0 also favoured carbonyl-rich polycycles, with sulfonylmorpholine-bearing aromatic appendages, and reached 0.2124137877466535. The new high families change the nitrogen-ring decoration while retaining that broad densely substituted character.
liabilities: Leading structures carry substantial molecular bulk, multiple carbonyl groups and complex ring junctions, which complicate synthesis and leave physical-property balance unestablished.
Cyclopropenyl sulfonyl groups and unusually contracted nitrogen-ring connectivity occur near the top; related simpler structures have similar scores.
Late analogues include aryl oxygen-fluorine groups. Saturated ring junctions and substituted carbonyl-containing rings lack explicit stereochemical specification.
missing_features: Less encumbered alternative cores that retain the useful nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic relationships are incompletely represented among the leaders. The simpler high-scoring ethylsulfonylpiperazine example is direct evidence that extensive fusion is not always necessary.

Defined stereochemistry and a consistent, synthetically credible treatment of ring contraction and fusion are absent from the elaborated saturated cores. A specific missing target substructure cannot be inferred from the observed score ceiling.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The more elaborated piperazine/sulfonyl/carbonyl assembly reaches 0.2024037172975581, while related structures with different core and sulfonyl connections score 0.2018354882632635. The seed-2 N-methylpiperazine polycycle reaches 0.1990553832983351. Crucially, the considerably simpler ethylsulfonylpiperazine attached to an aryl aza-lactam system scores 0.19835388147218586: the high tail does not require maximal fused-ring complexity. A late phenolic, carbonyl-rich molecule with a piperazine-containing side chain scores 0.18925686512914505. Together these suggest useful combinations of aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl environments, with only limited observed gains from extensive elaboration. The new upper values remain below the prior seed-0 best.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 produces compact bromobenzoyl azetidines bearing a dimethyltriazole and an amino, aminomethyl or hydrazino substituent. Another family contains bridged triazole-bearing nitrogen/oxygen rings. Seed 1 instead favours carbonyl-rich imidazolone/thione and related nitrogen/sulfur-ring chemistry, often with hydrazine or nitroso functionality and a halogenated phenyl group. Thus neither nitrogen heterocycles, saturated rings, amides nor primary amines are generally absent. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9845, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9362, halogen_rate 0.7552 and mean_smiles_length 46.0. Ordinary amino-substituted N-acyl azetidines are more plausible synthetic starting points than several leading N-fluorinated or nitroso-bearing variants. Prior seed 0 favoured amine-substituted unsaturated carbocycles attached to bridged nitrogen/oxygen systems and reached 0.31657990190491997. The new runs access different compact nitrogen-rich cores, while retaining problematic heteroatom connectivity in parts of the high tail.
liabilities: The leading azetidine contains both a nitrogen-nitrogen bond and a nitrogen-fluorine bond. Its relatively high score is not evidence of ordinary chemical stability.

Other high examples contain nitroso-bearing nitrogen chains, multiple adjacent carbonyl groups, sulfur-nitrogen bonds or bridged nitrogen-oxygen connectivity, all of which merit scrutiny before calling the molecules practical synthesis targets.

Several saturated cores admit configurational alternatives but contain no explicit stereocentre annotations; large late assemblies further complicate synthesis without retaining the high-score arrangement.
missing_features: Stable alternatives that preserve the successful local amino/heteroaryl/amide arrangement while replacing the reactive hydrazino or nitroso chemistry are not established at the leading score level. Conventional primary amine variants are present, so an absence-of-amines diagnosis would be false.
Configurationally specified azetidine and bridged-ring variants are missing from the emitted structures. The observations do not establish which configuration, if any, the objective would reward.
Core and substituent relocation frequently fail to preserve the narrow useful arrangement. The sampled molecules do not identify a uniquely required missing heterocycle or halogen pattern.

Its fluoromethyl-substituted hydrazino counterpart, which has carbon-bound fluorine rather than the same nitrogen-fluorine bond, scores 0.32889377886677046. The otherwise related aminomethyl and amino examples score 0.28462019114736514 and 0.27965004712778896. A separate nitroso-bearing carbonyl heterocycle reaches 0.3051477892817265. Location and connectivity matter: placing an N-fluorohydrazino substituent on the triazole while retaining the azetidine aminomethyl group gives only 0.0009072140941170833. The bulky polycyclic, polyol-containing low-tail conjugate scores 0.0, and a very large halogenated aromatic/tetrazole assembly scores 2.0625181207397576e-74. The final ring-expanded dicarbonyl/triazole structure scores 0.02556661875964576. The visible preference is for a compact and specific nitrogen/amide/aryl arrangement, with particularly sharp penalties for some elaborations; nitrogen or fluorine addition alone is not a supported rule. The pooled median is 0.001511 despite the substantially higher leading examples.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high tails contain an aryl hypochlorite scoring 0.49263201457052164, an aryl sulfur-chlorine derivative scoring 0.4686060677105447, and an N-fluorohydrazino azetidine scoring 0.3532645847815139. Other cited examples include oxygen-fluorine bonds and nitroso-bearing nitrogen chains. Conventional phenol, amide and primary amine alternatives also occur. These examples show that reactive connectivity survives even among favourable accepted observations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically credible functional-group connectivity when modifying useful molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable functional-group replacements available while retaining the surrounding aryl, amine and carbonyl relationships. Distinguish carbon-bound halogen changes from halogenating oxygen, nitrogen or sulfur, and compare chemically coherent alternatives through the current session's accepted feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited low tails include methane and hydrazine at 0.0, tiny fluorinated heteroatom fragments at 0.0, and oversized polyaryl or polyfunctional conjugates with extremely small scores. Conversely, some relatively large piperazine/carbonyl structures occupy a high tail, while a simpler ethylsulfonylpiperazine/aza-lactam structure scores 0.19835388147218586 near more elaborate relatives. The evidence supports context-dependent size and connectivity requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Control of molecular size and connectivity is uneven: useful cores are sometimes fragmented away or expanded into overly elaborate assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent molecular core and useful local functional-group relationships. Explore size around accepted structures without relying on either repeated fragmentation or concatenation, and let feedback determine useful complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Cited triazolyl azetidines, bridged nitrogen/oxygen cores, substituted saturated amine rings and carbonyl-rich ring junctions can have configurational alternatives. Some leading structures also contain unusually short closures across aromatic frameworks or contracted ring systems. Abundant ring-closure markers therefore establish ring presence, not well-defined or accessible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical specification and provides inconsistent geometric control over new ring closures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configurational alternatives and chemically credible ring closure, expansion and contraction moves around useful molecular arrangements. Treat changes of saturation, junction geometry and linker shape as distinct chemical possibilities for feedback to assess. The present observations establish missing representation, not a demonstrated score benefit from any particular configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied leaders repeatedly revisit related biaryl-pyrazole or quinoline-urea cores, imine/acylhydrazone-linked heteroaromatics, aryl saturated-amine architectures, piperazine-bearing carbonyl polycycles, and N-acyl azetidines. Different seeds reach visibly different core families, showing that the generator can change scaffold, but much of each leading neighbourhood consists of decoration, local ring edits or further assembly of those families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of chemically distinct useful cores remains uneven within runs, despite abundant unique molecular identities and an overall varied repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted scaffold families and enable core replacements that preserve useful spatial relationships among donors, acceptors, amines and aromatic groups. Assess diversity in the chemistry of the cores and their functional-group arrangement rather than treating a new molecular string or peripheral substituent as sufficient coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Accessible saturated amines in aryl/linker arrangements accompany scores such as 0.9999986918258995, while a nitro-containing aromatic molecule that also has a primary amine scores 8.914135292267243e-05. In another local family, the N-fluorohydrazino azetidine scores 0.3532645847815139, but a structure carrying that type of substituent on the triazole while retaining an aminomethyl group scores 0.0009072140941170833. These are whole-molecule observations, but they directly contradict a simple more-nitrogen or more-fluorine interpretation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group placement is not reliably conserved when exploring favourable amine and heteroaryl chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and vary functional-group attachment context, spacing and electronic environment deliberately. Make changes to a free amine, an amide nitrogen, a ring nitrogen and an imine distinct chemical operations so accepted feedback can reveal useful local arrangements without repeatedly losing them during unrelated growth.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

activation_observables.measurement: Audit every fit's ordered molecular identities, origins and score targets against earlier accepted observations from the same session, with zero unaccepted pool members or future labels. Reconstruct the fingerprint posterior from the logged normalization, kernel, noise and actual jitter. The Parent has no posterior fit. On each later genetic fit, compare predictions on the identical molecules selected at the preceding fit against their stored pre-feedback predictions; report fit count, training-set growth and nonzero fixed-probe prediction displacement. Include intervening accepted policy samples as ordinary training data. Exclude terminal feedback without a later genetic suggestion from update opportunities.
activation_observables.name: accepted_only_fingerprint_posterior_feedback

activation_observables.measurement: For every posterior-selected genetic slot, reconstruct the full correlated function draw from its logged standard-normal vector and conditional covariance and verify that the emitted identity is its maximum over the available pool mask. Report selected sampled value minus the available-pool mean, sample-rank enrichment relative to uniform selection, and the number and fraction of positive nondegenerate margins. Compare selected identities with the first m generation-order candidates from that exact pool, where m is the batch's number of selectable slots. approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates a learned molecule sampler with ordinary graph breeding. An autoregressive SMILES model is first trained on unlabeled molecules and kept as a frozen prior. Each objective gets an adaptable copy that generates one batch, followed by two batches made through graph crossover and atom or bond edits. Accepted neural samples refresh a scored population of up to sixty-four molecules, and a fresh neural sample is forced to participate in breeding at each handoff. Accepted graph descendants then train the adaptable sampler through score-ranked replay, trajectory balance with a learned normalizer, and regularization toward the frozen prior. This reciprocal loop ran repeatedly, but each valid novel graph descendant was sent directly for evaluation, and most scored below its best generating parent.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection to the genetic phase. The first forced neural-parent offspring at each handoff stays as in the Parent, so the reciprocal exchange remains intact. finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection and reciprocal feedback reproduce across seeds; offspring efficiency remains weak
finding_summary.insights: Replication rules out missing selector execution or a broken reciprocal handoff as explanations for the weak offspring yield: both mechanisms remain active across all three seeds. It also weakens the original suggestion of improved average child-minus-parent score, which held on the screening seed but not on the two additional seeds. The selector consistently changes which offspring are evaluated, but this does not establish that uncertainty itself improves final scores. The original direct-submission Parent has only one available seed, so the earlier paired score gain of 0.005848 remains a single-seed comparison; the new results establish repeatable execution and describe score variability without establishing a paired multi-seed improvement. Prediction error in the new runs is lower than an archive-mean baseline on four of five objectives, yet nominal 95% latent intervals cover only 80.4% of selected accepted scores overall and 41.9% on sitagliptin_mpo, where prediction MSE is also worse than that baseline. The molecular assessment shows that ring systems and useful basic-amine chemistry are already available, while leading families still mix conventional scaffolds with reactive substitutions, complicated connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry. That narrows the remaining questions toward reliable discrimination among chemically credible alternatives and broader useful scaffold coverage. Matched Parent replicas and a same-pool mean-only or direct-order comparison are still needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency and uncertainty's contribution.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich scaffold families with useful saturated amines, unresolved stereochemistry, and unusual reactive groups among the leaders
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Node n-cc2d839e347b produced recognisable medicinal-chemistry motifs: indole carboxamides, heteroaryl ketones, fused cyclic tertiary amines, sulfonylmorpholines, cyclic lactams and oxygen-bridged polycycles. All five trajectories are available, each with 300 records including 290 optimizer proposals. Proposal ring-closure presence rates are 0.9828 to 0.9931 and aromatic-atom presence rates are 0.9448 to 0.9724. These text counters measure whether a molecule contains the feature, not its ring count, aromatic atom fraction or three-dimensionality. Saturated and partly saturated rings are prominent in several leading families. The stereocentre-marker rate is nevertheless 0.0 everywhere, including molecules with asymmetric ring junctions and substituted oxetanes. Mean SMILES lengths range from 42.3 to 68.3; those are text lengths, not molecular weights. Each task has 300 unique molecules, but its leading examples concentrate in related scaffold families, which motivates the narrow diversity judgement. Ordinary amide, amine, ether and sulfonamide chemistry coexists with thioketenes, ketenimines, unusual N-O/N-S bonds, highly unsaturated oxygen rings and difficult bridged structures. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed. All interpretations below concern the supplied seed-0 molecules and recorded scores; stability, synthesis, binding and a score benefit from untested missing features were not measured.

Later leaders add N-amino or N-sulfanyl substitution to the amide nitrogen and replace the ordinary vinyl group with a thioketene or ketenimine. approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates a learned molecule sampler with ordinary graph breeding. An autoregressive SMILES model is first trained on unlabeled molecules and kept as a frozen prior. Each objective gets an adaptable copy that generates one batch, followed by two batches made through graph crossover and atom or bond edits. Accepted neural samples refresh a scored population of up to sixty-four molecules, and a fresh neural sample is forced to participate in breeding at each handoff. Accepted graph descendants then train the adaptable sampler through score-ranked replay, trajectory balance with a learned normalizer, and regularization toward the frozen prior. This reciprocal loop ran repeatedly, but each valid novel graph descendant was sent directly for evaluation, and most scored below its best generating parent.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection to the genetic phase. A Gaussian process learned from this objective's accepted scores uses molecular fingerprints to draw plausible score functions over a fresh pool of offspring from the existing graph operators. Each available evaluation slot takes the best remaining offspring under a new sampled function. The first forced neural-parent offspring at each handoff stays as in the Parent, so the reciprocal exchange remains intact. This lineage has only tested direct submission so far; the new ingredient is selection among genetic offspring before they receive real scores. A related graph-only experiment improved final best scores without improving its parent-beating rate, so the hypothesis here concerns discovering useful upper-tail outcomes within the reciprocal loop, with descendant efficiency measured separately.
